fatal_errors: The proposed Hf-to-Al substitution does not reconstruct the target intervention of adding 4.2 at.% Cr to form a reticulated multicomponent Laves phase.

The predicted 10–15% density reduction is inconsistent with replacing only 10–20% of the Hf sublattice; simple mass balance suggests a substantially smaller reduction unless 10–20 at.% of the entire alloy is replaced.
The cited evidence does not demonstrate that Al substitution in HfMoTaTiZr preserves strength and ductility near 1000 °C.
explanation: The hypothesis directly addresses density reduction and preservation of room- and high-temperature properties, and it supplies a controlled alloy series with quantitative rejection criteria. It is therefore a testable alternative rather than wholly unsupported. However, it misses the target Cr-addition intervention, the approximately 4 vol.% reticulated Cr2(Ti,Zr,Hf,Ta) Laves phase, and the coupled lattice-distortion and crack-deflection mechanism. Its phase-stability boundary is generic rather than tied to network morphology and lattice contraction. E2 shows that Al-containing refractory alloys can have low density, but it concerns a different alloy family and does not validate Hf-to-Al substitution or retention of properties at 1000 °C; E1 likewise does not support the proposed intervention. The experiment can test performance, but it does not strongly discriminate solid-solution strengthening from precipitation strengthening. The ambiguity between replacing 10–20% of Hf and adding 10–20 at.% Al also undermines the quantitative density prediction.
